mn63:2.12: ‘the cosmos is eternal’ or ‘the cosmos is not eternal’ …
mn63:2.13: or ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’—
mn63:3.2: “Sir, as I was in private retreat this thought came to my mind—
mn63:3.3: There are several convictions that the Buddha has left undeclared; he has set them aside and turned them down.
mn63:3.4: ‘the cosmos is eternal’ or ‘the cosmos is not eternal’ …
mn63:3.5: or ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’—
mn63:3.6: The Buddha does not explain these points to me.
mn63:3.7: I don’t endorse that, and do not accept it.
mn63:3.8: I’ll go to him and ask him about this.
mn63:3.9: If he gives me a straight answer on any of these points,
mn63:3.10: ‘the cosmos is eternal’ or ‘the cosmos is not eternal’ …
mn63:3.11: or ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’—
mn63:3.12: I will lead the spiritual life under him.
mn63:3.13: If he does not explain these points to me,
mn63:3.14: ‘the cosmos is eternal’ or ‘the cosmos is not eternal’ …
mn63:3.15: or ‘a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’—
mn63:3.16: I shall resign the training and return to a lesser life.
mn63:3.29: whether ‘the cosmos is finite’ or ‘the cosmos is infinite’, it is straightforward for someone who neither knows nor sees to simply say:
mn63:3.36: whether ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘the soul is one thing, the body another’, it is straightforward for someone who neither knows nor sees to simply say:
mn63:3.43: whether ‘a realized one still exists after death’ or ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’, it is straightforward for someone who neither knows nor sees to simply say:
mn63:3.48: that a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death, tell me.

mn63:6.7: When there is the view ‘the cosmos is finite’ or ‘the cosmos is infinite’, there is rebirth, there is old age, there is death, and there is sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
mn63:6.8: And it is the defeat of these things in this very life that I advocate.
mn63:6.11: When there is the view ‘the soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘the soul is one thing, the body another’, there is rebirth …
mn63:6.15: When there is the view ‘a realized one still exists after death’ or ‘a realized one no longer exists after death’, there is rebirth …
mn63:6.16: And it is the defeat of these things in this very life that I advocate.
mn63:10.8: The Shorter Discourse With Māluṅkyaputta is finished—the third.
